episodes.178698: A passing cold front generated some showers and thunderstorms that produced an outflow boundary with some strong winds.
episodes.178762: Locally induced afternoon thunderstorms on May 17th produced up to 3 inches of rain over portions of the southwest quadrant of Puerto Rico.
episodes.178781: A strong thunderstorm pushing offshore produced hail and gusty winds near Cape Canaveral.
episodes.178818: A severe thunderstorm developed just northwest of Rapid City and slowly drifted north and east through portions of the Rapid City, Black Hawk, and Summerset areas; producing hail around quarter size and heavy rain. Brief heavy rain and large amounts of small hail blocked storm drains and caused minor flooding across parts of Rapid City, with elevated stream levels on Rapid Creek east of Rapid City.
episodes.178819: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over far southeastern Fall River County, producing hail around quarter size southeast of Oelrichs.
episodes.178821: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northeastern Jackson County, producing wind gusts to 60 mph in the Belvidere area.
episodes.179234: A strong trough moved over the American Samoa islands on May 17th to cause widespread flash flooding in the region. The highest amount of rainfall recorded was from an ASPA (American Samoa Power Authority) weather station, which recorded 9.10 inches of rainfall at Fagaitua throughout the day. The majority of this rainfall came between 100 and 700SST. WSO Pago Pago received 2.83 inches during this time.
episodes.179294: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the area with a few reports of trees down across the Florida Big Bend and large hail in Jackson county.
episodes.179295: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the area with a few reports of trees down. In addition, a slow moving storm over Thomasville produced numerous reports of flash flooding.
episodes.179949: A surface cold front approaching from the north northwest in the afternoon was associated with a nearly west to east mid level shear axis streaking through the base of a large mid level trough whose low was centered over northern Quebec. Southwest flow ahead of this front drew in warm air and 60s dew points into the area, and this combined with strengthening mid level flow and upper divergence produced sufficient support for the development of numerous severe thunderstorms.
episodes.180216: A line of strong thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a nearby front during the late afternoon hours across southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms produced several instances of large hail and strong wind gusts.
episodes.180217: A line of strong thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a nearby front during the late afternoon hours across portions of southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms eventually moved into Charleston Harbor and produced strong wind gusts. Other thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast and produced strong wind gusts on Sapelo Island.
episodes.180240: An upper-level trough was across the eastern US with unsettled SW steering flow over the local forecast area. An old outflow boundary from prior convection moved across NE FL through the afternoon, which combined with sea breeze forcing and diurnal instability triggered a few strong to severe storms. Stronger dynamics (effective shear of 20-25 kts) and seasonably cool 500 mb temps (-10 degC) were across SE GA, but drier low-level air limited low-level instability and limited storm growth.
episodes.180241: An upper-level trough was across the eastern US with unsettled SW steering flow over the local forecast area. An old outflow boundary from prior convection moved across NE FL through the afternoon, which combined with sea breeze forcing and diurnal instability triggered a few strong to severe storms. Stronger dynamics (effective shear of 20-25 kts) and seasonably cool 500 mb temps (-10 degC) were across SE GA, but drier low-level air limited low-level instability and only enabled a few strong to isolated severe storms to develop in the late afternoon and into the evening near boundary merger.
episodes.180314: An unusually moist pattern for mid-May was in place over Arizona with precipitable water values around 200-250% of normal. This allowed for the development of strong to severe thunderstorms. Two thunderstorms produced severe hail on May 17 in different counties.
episodes.180370: A multi-day severe weather event unfolded across Central Alabama from May 16th through May 18th, 2023.  An active northwest flow pattern coupled with a stalled out surface frontal boundary provided the ingredients necessary for strong to severe thunderstorms to develop during the heating of the day.
episodes.180509: A region of low pressure pushed a strong cold front eastward and lifted a warm front northward through the Mid Atlantic during May 16. More than sufficient instability and shear in the Virginia Southside resulted in a few rounds of discrete thunderstorms that organized into a quasi-linear structure, which resulted in areas of thunderstorm wind damage and hail.
episodes.180543: A region of low pressure pushed a strong cold front eastward and lifted a warm front northward through the Mid Atlantic during May 16. More than sufficient instability and shear in North Carolina resulted in a few rounds of discrete thunderstorms that organized into a quasi-linear structure, which resulted in areas of thunderstorm wind damage and hail.
episodes.180547: Unseasonably moist air and weak instability fueled isolated thunderstorms around the Mojave Desert. One storm produced flooding.
episodes.180567: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeastern Colorado during the afternoon hours of May 16th. As they tracked east, they became severe as they approached Chase County. Hail up to one inch in diameter was reported in western Chase County.
episodes.180568: A cold front, tracking through western Nebraska, led to the development of thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours of May 17th. Some severe storms impacted northern Sheridan County where wind gusts up to 60 MPH and quarter size hail was reported.
episodes.180729: A severe thunderstorm developed over northwestern Natrona County and became severe as it moved southeastward.
episodes.180787: A line of thunderstorms developed across the western Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles during the afternoon of the 17th. East of this line was some unstable air where a discrete storm developed and dropped large hail over portions of northern Gray County. The largest hailstone reported was 1.75 6 miles south of Miami, TX.
episodes.180906: Scattered severe thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.180907: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.180908: Isolated severe thunderstorm along a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.180909: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.180973: Spring rains across the area resulted in additional high elevation snowmelt which led to elevated water levels along many creeks and streams. Belt Creek flooded for a second time this month. Water levels crested at 6.78 feet at the river gauge along Belt Creek near Monarch. Water briefly impacted Sluice Boxes State Park's entrance parking lot and flooded primarily fields and driveways from Sluice Boxes northward to near Armington. Two men visiting Sluice Boxes State Park were impacted by the fast moving water current associated with the high water levels and ultimately drown. Water levels were high all the way from near Belt to near Neihart.
episodes.181054: Strong storms developed across southwest Alabama during the afternoon and produced several reports of damage.
episodes.181063: During the afternoon a thunderstorm moved southeast out of Nebraska into Northwest Kansas.  The thunderstorm had produced severe wind gusts near Haigler, and continued to produce them as it moved southeast.  A peak gust of 67 MPH was measured near St. Francis.  Hail up to quarter size was reported in St. Francis from this storm.  Almost one and a half inches of rainfall was reported near St. Francis from this storm.  The high rainfall rate caused water to flow down the streets of St. Francis, becoming curb deep at the bottom of the hill in town.
episodes.181064: A thunderstorm was moving southeast across Dundy County.  As it moved into Northwest Kansas it produced wind gusts up to 68 MPH near Haigler.
episodes.181087: Thunderstorms formed along a stationary front in a very moist airmass. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rain that led to ponding of water and some flooded roads and intersections.
episodes.181123: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon on May 17th. One of those storms initiated over New Orleans before moving onto Lake Borgne. With the help of some boundaries over the lake, the storm was able to take advantage of the vorticity of the boundaries and produce a couple of waterspouts before moving south off of the lake 30 minutes later.
episodes.181147: Strong storms developed across southeast Mississippi during the afternoon and produced large hail.
episodes.181282: A prolonged period of well-below-average spring temperatures combined with an above-average winter snowpack created a dynamic breakup of the Yukon River. This resulted in numerous ice jams and snowmelt flooding on the Yukon River. Breakup flooding began on May 12th in eastern Alaska in Eagle and ended on June 3rd in the Yukon River delta at the Bering Sea coast. The primary cause of this active flood year was a 1-2 week delay in breakup when compared to typical timing. April temperatures were well below normal, and when temperatures began to warm in early May, it melted the low-elevation snowpack quickly. Because of the relatively quick addition of snowmelt onto strong ice, the ice was more susceptible to jamming and floods. In addition to the late breakup, the snowpack this winter was 1 to 1.5 times greater than the climatological normal for interior and western Alaska. Significant ice jams and associated flooding on the Upper Yukon River resulted in large volumes of ice and water to move down into the Middle Yukon River.
episodes.181396: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon across the North Carolina Blue Ridge. One of these quickly evolved into a severe supercell thunderstorm in McDowell County and tracked east/southeast to the Charlotte metro area, producing areas of large hail and damaging downbursts along its path, including a significant downburst in Cherryville. This was followed by a decaying line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved into the area from east Tennessee during mid-to-late evening and produced additional localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.181397: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon across the Blue Ridge escarpment and moved southeast. One of these produced isolated damaging wind gusts in Anderson County. This was followed by a decaying line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved into the area from the North Carolina mountains during late evening and produced additional localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.181448: Heavy rain from thunderstorm caused a debris flow near the Walker Creek Burn Scar.
episodes.182878: Heavy rain and snow melt led to a debris along Mad River.

Heavy rainfall also cause erosion underneath the road to create significant damage to the roadway making it impassible. There were no injuries.

The two men went into the fast moving water to retrieve their dog. The dog made it to shore, but the two men were pulled downstream and ultimately drowned. Water levels also flooded a portion of Sluice Boxes State Park's entrance parking lot as well as fields and yards from Sluice Boxes northward to Armington. A house in Neihart was flooded near the area were O'Brien Creek enters Belt Creek.
